text:
sam: heads-up — i'm piloting a 'decay baseline' cost guard for tenant canaries. goal: avoid noisy short-lived spikes pausing rollouts while still catching sustained cost regressions. thoughts?

maria: curious — how do you compute the baseline? p50 over last 24h or something fancier?

sam: good q. plan is EMA on per-tenant per-route token cost (tokens/request * model_unit_price) with 24h half-life + p50 fallback for sparse tenants. using decay means a sudden blip won't immediately double the baseline.

tj: API-level note: we need the evaluator to be pluggable. please don't hardcode EMA. can we expose `eval: {type: ema, params: {...}}` in the rollout guard schema so teams can swap in percentiles or custom funcs?

sam: exactly. thinking schema like: `guard: {id, type: cost, evaluator: {kind: "ema" | "percentile" | "script", config: {}} , threshold: float, action: pause|scale-down}`

kevin: telemetry angle — make sure we emit both raw_metric and evaluator_value as timeseries and histograms. otherwise console shows a pause but operators can’t see why. also we should record a "baseline_version" tag when evaluator config changes.

ui-ux: UI ask — when the guard pauses a canary can we show a short reason string and the contributing metric sparkline? e.g. "auto-pause: cost x2 vs EMA(24h)" and a link to the small explainer overlay. :eyes:

ops: question on behavior: pause vs rollback. i prefer automatic pause + notify + human-ack required to resume. rollback is scary without automated tests.

sam: agree. default action = pause + alert. optional `auto_rollback: true` for teams that opt in after safety checks.

infra-bot: deploy-check: canary guard v2 deployed to staging at 2023-11-02T17:02:13Z (sha: abc123).

maria: thought on thresholds — should thresholds be absolute multipliers (e.g. 2.0x baseline) or tenant-budget-aware (absolute $ per minute)? tenants with tiny spend might need different rules.

kevin: recommend both. config allows `threshold: {mode: multiplier, value: 2.0}` or `threshold: {mode: absolute, value: 0.75}` (USD/min). the evaluator emits both "baseline_usd_per_min" and "baseline_multiplier" so the guard can compare either.

tj: also add a cooldown window after resume where auto-pause is suppressed for X minutes unless metric continues to be high. otherwise flappy canaries.

sam: yep plan includes `min_pause_duration` and `grace_window` params.

ui-ux: UX for console: show current guard state in rollout timeline nodes. hover shows last 24h sparkline, evaluator config, and human override log. add an inline CTA: "open incident" prefilled with top metric snapshot.

ops: how will alerts route? we should surface tenant_id, route, guard_id, baseline_value, current_value, and last_sample_ts. also provide a presigned CSV of samples for debugging.

kevin: telemetry note — compute a rolling p95 latency for the evaluator query to avoid the guard choking control plane; if evaluator lag > 5s fallback to conservative safe-mode (pause off but escalate).

maria: small implement detail — for sparse tenants use cross-tenant priors: hierarchical decay that borrows strength from cohort mean when tenant sample count < N. otherwise baseline is noisy.

sam: good call. will add `prior_enabled: true` and `prior_weight` param.

ops: can we simulate the guard on historical traces before enabling? i want a dry-run UI that flags what would have paused.

sam: yes — feature request: console -> rollout -> "simulate guards" which runs evaluator on past 7/30 days and shows hypothetical hits. will add to backlog.

tj: quick config YAML example (for prototyping):
```
guard:
  id: cost_decay_v1
  type: cost_threshold
  evaluator:
    kind: ema
    params: {half_life_hours: 24}
  threshold:
    mode: multiplier
    value: 2.0
  action: pause
  min_pause_duration: 15m
  grace_window: 5m
  prior_enabled: true
  auto_rollback: false
```
kevin: love it. add `emit_debug_samples: true` for staging so we can inspect raw rows. remember to scrub PII.

ui-ux: one more UX point — make the pause reason discoverable in tenant billing pages so SRE/customer success can triage with customers.

sam: next steps: i'll wire the pluggable evaluator API, add EMA + percentile implementations, hook telemetry for evaluator_value + baseline, and push a staging rollout. canaries will start in the "simulate" mode for 48h then move to "active".

ops: tagging followups — @maria please draft guidance on threshold defaults per tenant tier. @ui-ux please mock the rollout timeline node. @kevin you'll add telemetry panels.

maria: on it.

ui-ux: will post mocks by EOD tomorrow.

kevin: i'll add the metrics and a dashboard wire.

infra-bot: note: staging simulation run started at 2023-11-02T17:15:02Z for guard cost_decay_v1.
